subject: NimbleNet — Annual commit slab options and next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference>
To: Nora Patel <nora@nimblenet.com>
Cc: Ethan Li <ethan.li@nimblenet.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: NimbleNet — follow-up and ask on annual commit sizing

Hi Nora,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciated the context on your latency-sensitive document extraction pipeline. Per our chat, you asked for a simple overview of annual commit tiers (Starter / Growth / Enterprise) and the expected per-token economics so you can take it into procurement.

Quick ask: could you share an approximate monthly token profile (avg tokens per request, peak qps, and estimated monthly calls)? I can sketch a slab-first proposal tailored to your usage shape, then we can iterate.

Proposed next steps:
- You send current monthly token estimate by Tue 7/13
- I send an initial commit tier proposal + worksheet (pdf + spreadsheet) by Fri 7/10
- If numbers look good, we route to procurement and DocuSign link for signature

Attaching a simple worksheet template I typically use. Low friction — we can make the Starter tier non-binding pilot if you want an easy ramp.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.inference | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: nimblenet-usage-scenario.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Nora Patel <nora@nimblenet.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference>
Cc: Ethan Li <ethan.li@nimblenet.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NimbleNet — follow-up and ask on annual commit sizing

Hi Camila,

Apologies for the delay — the token estimate below is high-level but should be OK to start:
- Current monthly: ~120M tokens (avg request ~400 tokens, ~1,000 requests/day)
- Peak forecast (Q4): ~350M tokens/month if we ship more OCR pipelines
- Retention: we expect steady growth ~20% q/q

Procurement will want: per-token price at Starter/Growth/Enterprise tiers, commitment term (12 months), and what happens if we exceed commit (overage pricing or carry-forward credits). Also need security notes on data retention and SOC2 artifact timelines, but that can be handled in parallel with security.

Would appreciate a clean PDF we can circulate.

Best,
Nora
Nora Patel
Head of Platform Partnerships, NimbleNet
nora@nimblenet.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference>
To: Nora Patel <nora@nimblenet.com>
Cc: Ethan Li <ethan.li@nimblenet.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NimbleNet — follow-up and ask on annual commit sizing

Nora — attaching the initial proposal PDF and a populated worksheet based on the estimates you provided. TL;DR summary below so procurement can skim: 

Summary (starter / growth / enterprise) — annual committed tokens and headline per-token unit price (USD):
- Starter: 120M annual commit (10M/mo equivalent) — $0.00022 / token (base)
- Growth: 600M annual commit (50M/mo equiv) — $0.00017 / token (5% off list)
- Enterprise: 2.4B annual commit (200M/mo equiv) — $0.00012 / token (10% off list + 1% additional rebate on overage usage >120% of commit)

Key contract points (short):
- Term: 12 months (auto-renew opt-in)
- Overage: charge at 1.25x committed rate unless a carry-forward credit is agreed upon; we can build a 3-month smoothing clause for seasonal spikes
- Ramp protection: free pilot allowance of 5M tokens during first 30 days for Starter and Growth to validate integration
- Security & compliance: SOC 2 in progress (available by request); Private deployment available for Enterprise if required

Attachments in this email: 20260710-nimblenet-commit-proposal.pdf (proposal) and populated nimblenet-usage-scenario.xlsx

If you'd like, we can offer an introductory 7% one-time credit on the first-year invoice for deals that sign within two weeks (expires 2026-07-24). I copied Markus to pick up the commercial approval queue.

Next step: procurement review + list of any contract redlines. If the numbers look close, I’ll prepare a DocuSign with the selected slab.

Thanks,
Camila

Attachments: 20260710-nimblenet-commit-proposal.pdf (proposal stub)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: NimbleNet draft — pricing approval + optional pilot credit

Folks — taking NimbleNet to procurement. Quick notes:
- Proposed list is Starter 120M / Growth 600M / Enterprise 2.4B as per my pdf.
- Asking for a 7% first-year sign-by credit if they commit within 2 weeks. Nora asked for clarity on overages & smoothing clauses.

Questions for pricing sign-off:
1) Can we make the overage cap at 1.15x for Enterprise instead of 1.25x if we commit to a 90-day smoothing window?
2) Do we want to attach a one-time onboarding credit (5% invoice credit) in addition to the sign-by credit for technical integration costs?

My recommendation: Approve the 7% incentive and set Enterprise overage to 1.15x with a 90-day smoothing clause — helps close this quarter.

Thanks — Camila

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.inference>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: NimbleNet draft — pricing approval + optional pilot credit

Camila — OK to proceed with the following changes:
- Approve the 7% sign-by credit (only for first-year committed invoice)
- Approve a one-time onboarding credit up to $12,000 (apply as invoice credit)
- Enterprise overage: lower to 1.15x committed rate if we include a 90-day smoothing clause; add language that any >150% sustained usage for more than 2 months triggers a re-rate discussion

Marking this approved; please update the PDF and send the DocuSign with the onboarding credit line item.

-Markus
Head of Sales, North America
markus.klein@redwood.inference
